title: Finite operation projection in intrinsic tensor coordinates
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, coefficient datum $C$ with prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $m\ge0$. Let $F$ be finite six-functor operations at exponent $m+1$ [def-sf-operation-stages]. For finite-type schemes $X,Y$ over the specified algebraic closure, a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$, a compactification $c$, arbitrary bounded constructible $K$ with coefficients $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{m+1}$ on $X$, and finite-Tor bounded constructible $L$ on $Y$, the intrinsic counit/open arrow finiteReductionProjection of [def-exchange-projection], evaluated in the normalized intrinsic derived tensor models is isomorphic to the ambient arrow underlying CompactSupportFiniteProjection.component for $F,f,c,K,L$ [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates]. Both inputs already have finite coefficients. No integral lift of either input, comparison between levels, or separated structure morphism is assumed.

source.place: Adic reconstruction and specified-map compatibility; presentation comparisons in the integral-stage reduction

proof.text: Expand the intrinsic compactification projection into its proper right-adjoint projection followed by proper image of the open projection isomorphism. Arrow.isoMk with identity source removes the latter. The tensorPullback_eq field identifies the proper component with finiteScalarProperProjection.
Apply finiteScalarProperProjection_presentation to c.g and the intrinsic extension-by-zero input. It compares the single proper counit factor, without any compactification or operation datum.

Localize finiteOpenIso and apply the exact derived composition comparisons. Apply the inverse realization and cancel its unit. This identifies the input with fixed-scalar extension by zero of the inverse realization of K. Naturality of the fixed proper projection gives its arrow isomorphism under this input comparison.

The fixed compactification projection is the fixed proper projection followed by two isomorphisms: proper image of inverse open projection and of the pullback compositor. Arrow.isoMk inserts these factors; map the resulting arrow isomorphism through realization.

The definition of component conjugates the realized fixed projection by sourceComparison.hom and targetComparison.inv. Arrow.isoMk on the inverse comparisons commutes by cancellation of sourceComparison. Compose all five arrow isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: B7 proper-factor reduction of the arrow-isomorphism statement: remove and insert the two open tails by their existing isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteProjection_operationPresentation
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] {m : ℕ}
    (F : SixFunctorFiniteOperations D C E (m + 1)
      (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le m)))
    {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f.hom.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom.left] [QuasiCompact f.hom.left]
    (c : Compactification f.hom.left)
    (K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E (m + 1)
      (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le m)) X)
    (L : finiteTorConstructibleCategory C.l E (m + 1)
      (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le m)) Y.obj.left) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk (finiteReductionProjection C.l E m c K.obj L.obj) ≅
      Arrow.mk (CompactSupportFiniteProjection.component F f c K L).hom)
